Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — project-takeover evaluation framework and benchmark ReqMemBench (349 requirement-diagnostic targets from 44 projects, 37 executable delivery targets from 7 projects) combining direct delivery, requirement-state diagnostics (RQ1-RQ3) and Oracle state conditions; six model-harness configurations (Codex CLI, Claude Code) compared under Full vs Relevant History and Oracle Pre-/Post-State

No SDD approach. Harnesses: Claude Code 2.1.283 (Claude Opus 5.5 claude-opus-5-5, Claude Sonnet 5 claude-sonnet-5) and Codex CLI 0.155.1 (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra), all high reasoning effort. Conditions: Full History (C1), Relevant History (C2, filtered by requirement annotations), Oracle Pre-State (gold pre-request requirement state supplied), Oracle Post-State (gold target requirement state supplied)

None prescribed by an SDD approach. Inputs: interaction history, current request, pre-request project environment. Requirement state per 'requirement atom' with five dimensions (attributes, lifecycle status, scope, ambiguity, implementation evidence); in Oracle conditions a restricted projection of the (predicted or gold) post-request requirement state (requirement ref, summary, state fields) is passed to coding. Responses follow schema rq-agent-response-v1

Direct delivery: read history + request, modify project, submit. Two-phase ReqMemBench protocol: Phase A requirement diagnostics (identify relevant requirements/evidence, reconstruct pre-request state, decide ACT/CLARIFY and output post-request state), response frozen; Phase B for ACT on execution-eligible targets: modify initial project using frozen response, then delivery checks. Oracle Pre-State: requirement update then coding; Oracle Post-State: coding from gold target

None during runs (agents run autonomously, permission mode dontAsk / sandbox settings). Humans only in benchmark construction: four reviewers in two pairs review Gold for all 44 projects and adjudicate flagged judge-label disagreements

Tasks: 37 executable delivery targets (7 projects) and 349 diagnostic targets (44 projects). Configurations: six model-harness pairs x conditions C1, C2, Oracle Pre-State, Oracle Post-State. Baseline: Full History (C1) as main condition. Held constant within a configuration: targets, requests, initial environments, tool permissions, budgets (900 s / 1,800 s), validators; high reasoning effort; shared semantic judge; harness defaults otherwise (temperature, seeds not overridden). Acceptance tests: hidden build/target/regression validators (initial env must pass build and regression and fail target). Repetitions: one run per configuration, target and condition (technical retries not counted). Human intervention: none; tool restrictions (no network, no other runs)

Complete delivery is low everywhere: mean 4.95% under C1 vs 2.70% under C2 (filtered history did not help); best C1 configuration Codex + GPT-6 Astra 10.81%, Claude Code + Sonnet 5 0%. Oracle Post-State raises mean complete delivery to 8.11% and build 58.56 -> 96.40%, regression 51.35 -> 90.99%, but target-test only 6.31 -> 9.01%; Oracle Pre-State 4.50%. No configuration produces any fully correct post-request state (0/312). Codex mean complete delivery (C1) 6.08% vs Claude Code 2.70%. No significance testing

Partly: it separates requirement understanding from implementation (Oracle conditions) and shows both fail; differences between configurations are small (0-4 successes of 37) and rest on one run without statistical tests. Authors' stated limits: only 37 executable tasks from 7 projects, six configurations with two harnesses, dependence on semantic judgement and annotation uncertainty

Limitations: executable validation covers only 37 tasks from 7 projects; six model-harness configurations (Codex CLI, Claude Code) limit representativeness; requirement boundaries, state values and free-text matching depend on semantic judgement, so annotation and scoring uncertainty remain. Future work: more projects and takeover points with recoverable environments, more models and harnesses. Gap: agents struggle both to form complete target requirement states and to implement supplied targets in existing projects

Gold RQ2/RQ3 structural/semantic review done by a single agent (SINGLE_AGENT_ROLE_SEPARATED_PANEL), then four human reviewers; candidate selection used GPT-5.6 Sol, which is also the semantic judge and one evaluated model.
